content.user_title: Build Reliable Elixir and Phoenix Systems
content.value_statement: Elixir projects require careful decisions about concurrency, supervision, data boundaries, testing, and performance. This skill provides focused guidance for idiomatic, fault-tolerant implementations.
actual_capabilities: Designs OTP applications using GenServer, Supervisor, and Application patterns.
Structures Phoenix applications with contexts and clean boundaries.
Guides LiveView features for real-time user interfaces.
Models database operations with Ecto changesets and explicit validation.
Creates ExUnit testing strategies with doctests, asynchronous tests, and property-based coverage.
Recommends Dialyzer, Benchee, Telemetry, Observer, and Recon practices.
limitations: It does not execute, compile, profile, or deploy an Elixir project by itself.
Recommendations require validation against the project version, dependencies, infrastructure, and production workload.
The packaged skill does not include the referenced implementation playbook.
It does not replace security review, database planning, or distributed systems testing.

use_cases.title: Structure a New OTP Service
use_cases.description: Plan process ownership, supervision boundaries, restart behavior, and test coverage for a new service.
use_cases.target_user: Elixir developers starting a production service

use_cases.title: Improve a Phoenix Application
use_cases.description: Review contexts, LiveView state, Ecto changesets, and application boundaries for maintainability.
use_cases.target_user: Phoenix teams refining an existing application

use_cases.title: Diagnose BEAM Performance
use_cases.description: Develop a measurement plan using Telemetry, Benchee, Observer, and Recon before changing system behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Elixir Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Elixir module for idiomatic pattern matching, guard clauses, clear errors, and testability. Explain each recommendation and propose focused tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants practical feedback on a small module.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Supervision Tree
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an OTP supervision tree for these workers and dependencies: [details]. Define ownership, restart strategies, failure boundaries, startup order, and ExUnit tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs a fault-tolerant process architecture.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a LiveView Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan this Phoenix LiveView feature: [requirements]. Separate context logic, Ecto validation, LiveView state, events, authorization checks, telemetry, and integration tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: A Phoenix team is adding an interactive database-backed workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Distributed Bottleneck
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these symptoms and measurements from a clustered Elixir system: [evidence]. Form hypotheses, rank risks, and design Observer, Recon, Telemetry, and Benchee experiments.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced team needs an evidence-based performance investigation.

output_examples.input: Design supervision for a queue consumer, connection pool, and metrics reporter.
output_examples.output: Recommended design: isolate the connection pool, supervise queue consumers dynamically, and keep metrics reporting independent. Test restart behavior and dependency loss.

output_examples.input: Review a LiveView that performs validation and database writes inside event handlers.
output_examples.output: Move business operations into a context, retain presentation state in LiveView, validate through changesets, enforce authorization, and test both context and interface behavior.

output_examples.input: Investigate rising scheduler utilization after traffic doubles.
output_examples.output: First correlate scheduler, mailbox, garbage collection, and latency metrics. Reproduce the workload, profile measured hotspots, benchmark isolated changes, and compare results.

best_practices: Provide Elixir, Erlang, Phoenix, Ecto, and dependency versions with each request.
Describe process ownership, expected failures, workload, and recovery requirements before selecting OTP patterns.
Validate recommendations with ExUnit, Dialyzer, benchmarks, telemetry, and representative production conditions.
anti_patterns: Do not add processes when a pure function or existing process already provides clear ownership.
Do not choose supervision strategies without defining expected failures and restart dependencies.
Do not optimize BEAM behavior before collecting representative measurements.

faq.question: Which Elixir topics does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers OTP, Phoenix, LiveView, Ecto, concurrency, distributed systems, testing, type specifications, performance, and observability.

faq.question: Can it generate complete production applications?
faq.answer: It can guide architecture and implementation, but every result requires project-specific integration, testing, security review, and deployment validation.

faq.question: Does it run Elixir tools?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides instructions and recommendations; tool execution depends on the available agent environment and user authorization.

faq.question: Can it help with Phoenix LiveView?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan state management, events, contexts, validation, authorization, telemetry, and testing for LiveView features.

faq.question: How should performance advice be used?
faq.answer: Start with measurements, reproduce the workload, test one hypothesis at a time, and compare benchmarks before changing production behavior.

faq.question: Does it support distributed Elixir systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides guidance for nodes, clustering, process isolation, fault tolerance, and horizontal scaling, subject to infrastructure-specific validation.
